answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making standing grow like a grove rather than appear on demand. Each identity earns trust only by carrying one cedar work-thread forward, step by step, where every step's input is the signed output of the last, so the work cannot be split across machines or run in parallel. Each extra identity adds another full thread of delay, so fakes cost calendar time no bulk purchase shortens. A violet marker, earned only at the end of a completed thread, is what peers check before trading, and abandoned threads forfeit a bond tied to that thread alone.
